SMTO-HTTP-0066 — One of the request's headers isn't allowed

GUID: 639dca85-177f-4687-8c4d-804ea1276cba
Slug: http-header-invalid
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • Web requests carry extra labeled details called headers. One of them has an invalid name or value, appears twice, or is one SMTO fills in itself, so the request wasn't sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to resend the request without Host, Content-Length, Connection or Transfer-Encoding headers, and without any header listed twice. SMTO sets these headers itself and refuses requests that try to set them too.
  2. If the request uses a saved connection, open it in Parameter Store and check Default header under Advanced connection settings, and the header name in the Authentication section, for the same problems. Headers saved in the connection are added to every request it makes.
  3. Replace any emoji, characters from non-Latin alphabets or line breaks in header values with plain text. Header values can only contain basic Western characters on a single line.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's request is sent and returns a result from the service.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't remove the sign-in header the service needs; fix only the header that is invalid.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Header validation rejected a request header, profile default header or authentication header name: the name is not a valid token, the value has control characters or is not Latin-1, a name is duplicated (ignoring case), or the header is one the transport manages (Host, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, Connection and similar).

What this means

  • A request or extracted header has invalid token/value syntax, duplicate case-insensitive names, unsupported encoding or a field reserved to transport/session handling. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A request or extracted header has invalid token/value syntax, duplicate case-insensitive names, unsupported encoding or a field reserved to transport/session handling.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare safe header names and value types with transport-owned exclusions; do not print secret header values.

How to fix it

  • Use unique token header names with Latin-1 values and no control characters. Remove Host, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, Connection, Keep-Alive, TE, Trailer, Upgrade and proxy headers from the request, the profile's default_headers and its auth header_name or headers so the runtime computes them.
  • Use unique valid header names and Latin-1 values. Remove Host, Content-Length and other transport-owned headers so the runtime can calculate them.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Unique valid headers and runtime authentication pass the final wire validation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
